issue_context.title: AIP-81 Add New Configuration to Set CLI Token Expiration Time
issue_context.body:
### Description

Add New Configuration to Set CLI Token Expiration Time.
The config should be set from api configs because it will be used in Simple Auth Manager to generate token for CLI.

### Use case/motivation

[AIP-81](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW/AIP-81+Enhanced+Security+in+CLI+via+Integration+of+API)

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [x] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

review_comments:
I followed the same convention here even my mind ping me was that routers. I think all should be routers since we are creating a router in each router file :) 

https://github.com/apache/airflow/tree/main/tests/api_fastapi/core_api/routes
https://github.com/apache/airflow/tree/main/tests/api_fastapi/execution_api/routes
Should we say `router` or `routers`? Not sure we will have more controller layer in this context :thinking:
I am happy to rename it `routes`, but then we should be consistent and do the same in `src`. I just want to use the same name in `src` and `tests`
Amazing, renamed the src to routes to be consistent

Ideally, these tests should be in `test_login` in `services`. Because they test the business logic that is contained in `services/login` now. And then in here `router/test_login` we should have 2 tests, one per endpoint, that are mocking `Login`. These tests should just check that the value returned by `Login` is passed through the wire

Make sense! Separated the service layer test and route test. Service one calls the service and route one using the `test_client`. I ended up with 4 tests though because mocking is a bit weird due to LoginResponse normally not returning HTTPException but raising them. It should be fine to have them separate
